ceiling_statement: Maximum auditability is: every trusted output ships with a certificate that binds it, via collision-resistant hash commitments, to the COMPLETE closure of its derivation (source bytes, code identity, pinned toolchain identity, configuration, ordering schedule), such that an independent third party holding only the certificate and the committed closure can, fully offline and with zero producer trust, byte-identically RECOMPUTE the output and compare it to the commitment. Auditability terminates at the commitment boundary: nothing outside the committed closure (e.g., what the publisher's web server 'really' served at capture time) is auditable in principle — the strongest attainable is a signed/witnessed capture receipt committing the bytes at ingestion.
derivation: Verification theory admits exactly two zero-trust offline verification modes: (a) recompute-and-compare the derivation, or (b) check a succinct cryptographic proof of it. Mode (b) cannot exceed (a) in assurance — it adds trust in the proof system's soundness and in a correct arithmetization of the full semantics, and arithmetizing an SBCL pipeline is infeasible today — so recompute-and-compare over committed inputs is the ceiling, which is precisely H8's form. The boundary claim is information-theoretic: two histories producing identical committed byte-closures are indistinguishable to any auditor, so no audit can attest to anything not captured in the commitment; past states of external sources are not replayable, hence capture receipts are the maximum for origin bytes. Completeness of the closure is the only free variable, and 'complete' is capped by what was committed — an audit is exactly as strong as the closure is total. Ceiling holds for ANY system under H1–H8 modulo standard collision-resistance of the hash (SHA-256).
attainment_mechanism: Generalize the pattern B0 already runs: one release-closure certificate = Merkle root (single seat: source/merkle-authority.lisp, RFC-6962 with domain separation) over {corpus fingerprint (source/corpus-fingerprint.lisp), toolchain manifest, all committed input bytes, all output bytes, gate-plenary manifest (systems/orchestrator-cli/gates-runner.lisp)}, hashed through the single hash seat (source/hash-authority.lisp), sealed by the Ed25519 authority chain (source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp). The verifier is the recompute-and-compare engine already proven in source/authority-evidence-replay.lisp (re-runs source→extraction→byte-equivalence, trusts no declared root) plus the independent re-verification spine systems/orchestrator-epistemic/release-spine.lisp — extended to recompute the WHOLE closure, not selected artifacts, with per-step before→after hash-chain checks (closing the consolidation-ledger aggregate-only weakness in source/consolidation-proof.lisp). All of this is SHA-256 + Ed25519 + SBCL: buildable today.
b0_gap: B0 map marks AX-13 a leading axis (PROOF_CARRYING: release-spine, L6 verifier, fail-closed gates-runner manifest whose :completed t is positive proof). Gap to ceiling: (1) verification is spread across several seats (release-spine, deploy-epistemic, gates-runner, verify-truth-gate) instead of one closure certificate; (2) some byte-identity claims are asserted in comments/tests, not recomputed; (3) wall-clock leaks into artifacts unless frozen (couples to AX-14); (4) consolidation replay verifies aggregate base/result hash + step count, not the per-step hash chain; (5) origin bytes enter un-attested (government-source.lisp), so the commitment boundary is currently weaker than the attainable signed-capture-receipt boundary (B0 map §3, AX-04).
lean_obligation: Theorem (replay soundness+completeness at the ceiling): given an injective-on-domain commitment function H and a pure derivation function f (from AX-14), for all closures c and outputs o: Verify(cert(c,o), c) = true ↔ f(c) = o. Corollary (audit factorization): for all histories h₁ h₂, committedClosure(h₁) = committedClosure(h₂) → auditVerdict(h₁) = auditVerdict(h₂), i.e., the audit relation factors through the commitment — formalizable in Lean 4 as a function `verify : Cert → Closure → Output → Bool` with `∀ c o, verify (mkCert c o) c o = true ↔ derive c = o` under a `Function.Injective H` hypothesis on the committed domain.
